My energy has never shot up like that, and I've never felt extremely energetic or gone without needing sleep. It has really just been the opposite with this constant, drained feeling.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that this is your first episode of feeling this low and drained, lasting about three years, but can you tell me if you're concerned that you might experience another episode like this in the future, or if you're worried about your symptoms returning if they were to improve?\n\nPatient: Honestly, I haven't really thought about the future or the symptoms returning. Right now, I'm just focused on trying to get through this daily fog and find a way to get back to my normal self.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any changes in your energy levels, such as fatigue, or changes in your physical activity, like slowed movements or restlessness, over the past three years?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've felt constantly fatigued and drained over the last three years, often waking up already exhausted in the morning. While I haven't noticed specific restlessness or slowed movements, my physical activity has definitely decreased because I only have the energy to work and crash on the couch, which led me to drop activities like my softball games.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've experienced this low, drained feeling for about three years without any significant relief, do you think if you were to experience a period of improvement, you would be likely to have another episode of feeling this way in the future?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about that, as I haven't thought that far ahead yet. Right now, I'm just focusing on trying to feel better and get some of my energy back.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel this low, drained, and empty, and were able to enjoy activities and feel like your old self, even if it was just for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, I definitely haven't had a break of two months or more from these feelings. Ever since my routes changed about three years ago, this low, drained, and empty state has been my constant normal, without any periods where I felt like my old self or truly enjoyed things.\n\nDoctor: You've had this continuous low, drained feeling for about three years, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle differences in how you've experienced this feeling over time, such as changes in how it affects your daily life or your interest in activities?\n\nPatient: At first, I tried to keep up with volunteering and softball despite the new schedule, but I gradually got so worn down that I withdrew, spending my off-time alone or tinkering with my car instead of seeing friends.
